raw_draft.tldr: CBOT soybeans read price-supportive into the turn of the year: the US balance sheet is tight at a 10.72% stocks-to-use ratio for 2026/27 [N76], its 23rd percentile and falling three straight years [N78], with crush economics firm at a 2.43 USD/bu board crush margin [N109] and shipments running ahead at 775.39 thousand MT in the week to 17 September 2026 [N126] -- thirteen of the readings served here settle toward a higher price against six toward a lower one, beside a November 2026 delivery settle of 1,317.5 US cents/bushel [N1]. The counterweight is real and named: the tropical Pacific is at +1.8 degC in July 2026 [N16], a warm phase the model signs against soybeans, and managed money sits at the 100th percentile of its own record since August 2023 [N27], which the model reads as reversal risk, not as added fuel. On the three-month horizon the record gives no price range -- the chain from macro demand into soybeans answers the question, but the front price does not reach back to the past times these readings sat this far out.
raw_draft.mechanism:
## Mechanism

The physical chain is a demand-pull crush story sitting on a thin cushion. Crush value, not a weather shock, is doing the pulling: firm energy and biofuel demand lift the oil side of the crush, wide crush margins make processors bid for beans, and the drawn-down carryout leaves little slack to absorb any further call on supply. The model signs the tight stocks-to-use ratio as price-supportive at high confidence, the crush margin as price-supportive at high confidence, and a fast export pace as price-supportive at high confidence. Those three point the same way.

Against them: a strong warm phase in the tropical Pacific, which the model signs against soybeans at medium confidence with a one-to-two-quarter lag -- the channel is better South American yields, expanding crushable supply. Harvested area is also signed as loosening, at medium confidence. And the crowd is the wrinkle -- the positioning card reads an extreme position as large managed-money net length that amplifies and can overextend price moves, while extreme positioning flags reversal risk. I lean supportive because the balance-sheet and crush legs are high-confidence and already measured, while the warm-phase leg is medium-confidence and works through a South American crop not yet made. That is a model ranking, not a measured attribution.

Two convergence patterns are partly showing and neither is at its threshold: the crush demand-pull pattern names four conditions and one is counted here; the South American weather squeeze names five and one is counted here (the tight stocks-to-use ratio), with drought and heat stress carrying no series read on this turn. The supply-glut pattern is worse off still -- one condition showing, and the stocks-to-use reading counts against it.

## The record

Balance sheet, known 2026-09-11: 2026/27 ending stocks 310 Million Bushels [N9] against 325 Million Bushels for 2025/26 [N3]; stocks-to-use 10.72% [N11], at the 23rd percentile of its own record [N78]. USDA's own read of 2026/27 is a projection, not a settled year: average farm price 12 $/bu [N10] against the 2025/26 estimate of 10.5 $/bu [N4].

Drivers, in the chain order the record carries. Macro demand: no series is served at this link, and the model expects it to tighten the stocks-to-use ratio, with the readings not settling it; the dated action behind it is Mexico removing soybean oil from its anti-inflation decree in December 2025, still inside the lag the model allows [E19]. Stocks-to-use at 10.72% [N76], 23rd percentile [N78], falling since 2023 -- the model expects this to pull managed money the other way, and the readings agree. Managed money at 265,159 contracts [N25], +2.2 sigma [N26], 100th percentile [N27] -- the model expects it to move price the same way with a zero-to-one-quarter lag, and the readings do not settle it. The record is thin at that last link: it holds no past time positioning sat this far out with a price reading to measure, and the front price does not reach back.

The energy-side chain agrees where it can be measured: Brent against its own five-year record peaked at the 98th percentile in April 2026 [N116] and reads 0.51 z [N113] at the 68th [N115]; the model expects that to lift the board crush margin, and the readings agree. Of the past times Brent sat this far out, eight had a crush reading to measure -- five moved as the model expects, three the other way; eight more had no reading inside the lag. The crush peaked at the 96th percentile in July 2026 [N112], now the 89th [N111]. Dated report behind that link: soybean oil prices projected to rise by 8 percent in 2026, published 1 April 2026 [E39].

Other current readings: export shipments 775.39 thousand MT [N126], having bottomed at the 3rd percentile in August 2026 [N129] and now the 62nd [N128], rising three weeks; Argentine exports 6.45 MMT for 2026/27 [N117]; harvested area 34.76 M ha [N94] at the 91st percentile [N96]; US dry-spell length at -0.69 z [N37], the wetter side, 11th percentile [N39]. Price: November 2026 delivery settled 1,317.5 US cents/bushel [N1] -- the front-month rule could not run because open interest is not yet published for the session, so this is the nearest listed delivery outside its delivery month, not "the front month." World Bank soybeans August 2026: 482 USD/mt [N12].

Dated context, 2026: US soybean exports for 2026/27 raised 30 million bushels on stronger global demand, reported 10 July 2026 [E29]; global oilseed crush projected up 4 percent in 2026/27, reported 12 May 2026 [E5]; strong Chinese demand fuelled record Brazilian area for 2025/26 [E30]. Dry conditions in March and April 2026 depleted soil moisture in northeastern countries [E33], a window now closed.

The cross-market record from the 2025-01 to 2025-04 episode, an older window, read one way per pair: CBOT soybeans -3.18% [N168] against ZCE rapeseed meal +2.54% [N169] -- the declared same-direction demand-competition relation sat at odds over that window, read on each board's own currency, US dollars and Chinese yuan, with the yuan-per-dollar rate +0.32% [N170] inside that comparison and not removed from it. Soybeans against ZCE rapeseed oil +10.06% [N171] also sat at odds, same currency caveat. Soybeans against CBOT soybean meal -6.64% [N172]: the crush relation held. Soybean meal against soybean oil +4.01% [N173]: the declared opposite-direction relation held. Soybean oil against CME palm oil +4.8% [N174]: held. MATIF rapeseed cannot be read -- that window predates the board's own price history.

Season-average farm price across the analogue years, USDA survey actuals and not futures settles: fell from $12.40/bu [N166] in MY2023/24 to $10.00/bu [N167] in MY2024/25.

Recency: figures read as of 2026-09-29, newest known 2026-09-28, oldest 2026-04-09; the newest dated document is 2026-08-12; the board price tape runs through 2026-09-28.

## Where the record disagrees

The measured record splits on this exact chain. Over the 2025-01 to 2025-04 window the model's soy-to-rapeseed demand-competition links sat at odds -- soybeans fell 3.18% [N168] while ZCE rapeseed meal rose 2.54% [N169] and ZCE rapeseed oil rose 10.06% [N171] -- while every link inside the crush complex held: meal -6.64% [N172], oil +4.01% [N173], palm +4.8% [N174]. Read that as: the crush identity transmits reliably; the cross-oilseed substitution link did not, in-sample, on that window only.

## Cross-commodity

The largest moves carried here are also declared on five other markets -- CBOT soybean meal, CME palm oil, DCE palm olein, DCE soybean meal and ICE cocoa -- each with its own sign and lag. The warm Pacific phase is declared to move CME palm oil and DCE palm olein in the same direction at two-to-four quarters, high confidence; and ICE cocoa in the same direction at one-to-three quarters, medium confidence. Fishmeal substitution, the single largest move on the panel at 4.24 z [N13], 100th percentile of its record since September 2015 [N15], is declared on CBOT soybean meal and DCE soybean meal in the same direction at zero-to-two quarters, medium confidence -- a protein-complex pull that reaches beans through meal.

## What to watch

- **The Pacific warm phase** [N16]: +1.8 degC, July 2026, eight straight months rising, past the strong line at one and a half degC. Its window runs 2026-10-31 to 2027-01-31; next print between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-05. Wrong if that print turns back inside the line or the run breaks. This is the reading set against the supportive lean.
- **Board crush** [N109]: 2.43 USD/bu, 23 September 2026, three declared paths run through it onto the price. Window 2026-09-23 to 2026-12-23. Wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its own record. This prints every session and is the only carried reading that can genuinely turn inside three months.
- **Export shipments** [N126]: 775.39 thousand MT, week to 17 September 2026, past the ahead line, three weeks rising. Window 2026-09-17 to 2026-12-17; next print 2026-10-01. Wrong if it turns back inside that line or the run breaks.
- **Fishmeal** [N13]: 4.24 z, August 2026, top decile. Window 2026-08-01 to 2027-02-01. Wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its record.
- **US dry-spell length** [N37]: -0.69 z, August 2026, the wetter side; two declared upstream paths land on price through it. Window 2026-08-31 to 2026-11-30. Wrong if it returns to the middle of its record.

Weighed and left: the stocks-to-use ratio [N76] and harvested area [N94] are both past declared lines, but their next print on 2026-10-09 restates a period already reported -- standing context inside a three-month horizon, not a watch item. Scheduled publication dates are the publishers' and stay in the record's own note.

**TL;DR.** CBOT soybeans read price-supportive into the turn of the year: the US balance sheet is tight at a 10.72% stocks-to-use ratio for 2026/27 [N11], its 23rd percentile and falling three straight years [N78], with crush economics firm at a 2.43 USD/bu board crush margin [N109] and shipments running ahead at 775.39 thousand MT in the week to 17 September 2026 [N126] -- thirteen of the readings served here settle toward a higher price against six toward a lower one, beside a November 2026 delivery settle of 1,317.5 US cents/bushel [N1]. The counterweight is real and named: the tropical Pacific is at +1.8 degC in July 2026 [N16], a warm phase the model signs against soybeans, and managed money sits at the 100th percentile of its own record since August 2023 [N27], which the model reads as reversal risk, not as added fuel. On the three-month horizon the record gives no price range -- the chain from macro demand into soybeans answers the question, but the front price does not reach back to the past times these readings sat this far out.

## Mechanism

The physical chain is a demand-pull crush story sitting on a thin cushion. Crush value, not a weather shock, is doing the pulling: firm energy and biofuel demand lift the oil side of the crush, wide crush margins make processors bid for beans, and the drawn-down carryout leaves little slack to absorb any further call on supply. The model signs the tight stocks-to-use ratio as price-supportive at high confidence, the crush margin as price-supportive at high confidence, and a fast export pace as price-supportive at high confidence. Those three point the same way.

Against them: a strong warm phase in the tropical Pacific, which the model signs against soybeans at medium confidence with a one-to-two-quarter lag -- the channel is better South American yields, expanding crushable supply. Harvested area is also signed as loosening, at medium confidence. And the crowd is the wrinkle -- the positioning card reads an extreme position as large managed-money net length that amplifies and can overextend price moves, while extreme positioning flags reversal risk. I lean supportive because the balance-sheet and crush legs are high-confidence and already measured, while the warm-phase leg is medium-confidence and works through a South American crop not yet made. That is a model ranking, not a measured attribution.

Two convergence patterns are partly showing and neither is at its threshold: the crush demand-pull pattern names four conditions and one is counted here; the South American weather squeeze names five and one is counted here (the tight stocks-to-use ratio), with drought and heat stress carrying no series read on this turn (a served reading bears on this: [N130] = 0.11 z, August 2026, read 2026-09-05). The supply-glut pattern is worse off still -- one condition showing, and the stocks-to-use reading counts against it.

## The record

Balance sheet, known 2026-09-11: 2026/27 ending stocks 310 Million Bushels [N9] against 325 Million Bushels for 2025/26 [N3]; stocks-to-use 10.72% [N11], at the 23rd percentile of its own record [N78]. USDA's own read of 2026/27 is a projection, not a settled year: average farm price 12 $/bu [N10] against the 2025/26 estimate of 10.5 $/bu [N4].

Drivers, in the chain order the record carries. Macro demand: no series is served at this link, and the model expects it to tighten the stocks-to-use ratio, with the readings not settling it; the dated action behind it is Mexico removing soybean oil from its anti-inflation decree in December 2025, still inside the lag the model allows [E19]. Stocks-to-use at 10.72% [N11], 23rd percentile [N78], falling since 2023 -- the model expects this to pull managed money the other way, and the readings agree. Managed money at 265,159 contracts [N25], +2.2 sigma [N26], 100th percentile [N27] -- the model expects it to move price the same way with a zero-to-one-quarter lag, and the readings do not settle it. The record is thin at that last link: it holds no past time positioning sat this far out with a price reading to measure, and the front price does not reach back.

The energy-side chain agrees where it can be measured: Brent against its own five-year record peaked at the 98th percentile in April 2026 [N116] and reads 0.51 z [N113] at the 68th [N115]; the model expects that to lift the board crush margin, and the readings agree. Of the past times Brent sat this far out, eight had a crush reading to measure -- five moved as the model expects, three the other way; eight more had no reading inside the lag. The crush peaked at the 96th percentile in July 2026 [N112], now the 89th [N111]. Dated report behind that link: soybean oil prices projected to rise by 8 percent in 2026, published 1 April 2026 [E39].

Other current readings: export shipments 775.39 thousand MT [N126], having bottomed at the 3rd percentile in August 2026 [N129] and now the 62nd [N128], rising three weeks; Argentine exports 6.45 MMT for 2026/27 [N117]; harvested area 34.76 M ha [N94] at the 91st percentile [N96]; US dry-spell length at -0.69 z [N37], the wetter side, 11th percentile [N39]. Price: November 2026 delivery settled 1,317.5 US cents/bushel [N1] -- the front-month rule could not run because open interest is not yet published for the session, so this is the nearest listed delivery outside its delivery month, not "the front month." World Bank soybeans August 2026: 482 USD/mt [N12].

Dated context, 2026: US soybean exports for 2026/27 raised 30 million bushels on stronger global demand, reported 10 July 2026 [E29]; global oilseed crush projected up 4 percent in 2026/27, reported 12 May 2026 [E5]; strong Chinese demand fuelled record Brazilian area for 2025/26 [E30]. Dry conditions in March and April 2026 depleted soil moisture in northeastern countries [E33], a window now closed.

The cross-market record from the 2025-01 to 2025-04 episode, an older window, read one way per pair: CBOT soybeans -3.18% [N168] against ZCE rapeseed meal +2.54% [N169] -- the declared same-direction demand-competition relation sat at odds over that window, read on each board's own currency, US dollars and Chinese yuan, with the yuan-per-dollar rate +0.32% [N170] inside that comparison and not removed from it. Soybeans against ZCE rapeseed oil +10.06% [N171] also sat at odds, same currency caveat. Soybeans against CBOT soybean meal -6.64% [N172]: the crush relation held. Soybean meal against soybean oil +4.01% [N173]: the declared opposite-direction relation held. Soybean oil against CME palm oil +4.8% [N174]: held. MATIF rapeseed cannot be read -- that window reaches back before our own price history for that market.

Season-average farm price across the analogue years, USDA survey actuals and not futures settles: fell from $12.40/bu [N166] in MY2023/24 to $10.00/bu [N167] in MY2024/25.

Recency: figures read as of 2026-09-29, newest known 2026-09-28, oldest 2026-04-09; the newest dated document is 2026-08-12; the board price tape runs through 2026-09-28.

## Where the record disagrees

The measured record splits on this exact chain. Over the 2025-01 to 2025-04 window the model's soy-to-rapeseed demand-competition links sat at odds -- soybeans fell 3.18% [N168] while ZCE rapeseed meal rose 2.54% [N169] and ZCE rapeseed oil rose 10.06% [N171] -- while every link inside the crush complex held: meal -6.64% [N172], oil +4.01% [N173], palm +4.8% [N174]. Read that as: the crush identity transmits reliably; the cross-oilseed substitution link did not, in-sample, on that window only.

## Cross-commodity

The largest moves carried here are also declared on five other markets -- CBOT soybean meal, CME palm oil, DCE palm olein, DCE soybean meal and ICE cocoa -- each with its own sign and lag. The warm Pacific phase is declared to move CME palm oil and DCE palm olein in the same direction at two-to-four quarters, high confidence; and ICE cocoa in the same direction at one-to-three quarters, medium confidence. Fishmeal substitution, the single largest move on the panel at 4.24 z [N13], 100th percentile of its record since September 2015 [N15], is declared on CBOT soybean meal and DCE soybean meal in the same direction at zero-to-two quarters, medium confidence -- a protein-complex pull that reaches beans through meal.

## What to watch

- **The Pacific warm phase** [N16]: +1.8 degC, July 2026, eight straight months rising, past the strong line at one and a half degC. Its window runs 2026-10-31 to 2027-01-31; next print between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-05. Wrong if that print turns back inside the line or the run breaks. This is the reading set against the supportive lean.
- **Board crush** [N109]: 2.43 USD/bu, 23 September 2026, three declared paths run through it onto the price. Window 2026-09-23 to 2026-12-23. Wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its own record. This prints every session and is the only carried reading that can genuinely turn inside three months.
- **Export shipments** [N126]: 775.39 thousand MT, week to 17 September 2026, past the ahead line, three weeks rising. Window 2026-09-17 to 2026-12-17; next print 2026-10-01. Wrong if it turns back inside that line or the run breaks.
- **Fishmeal** [N13]: 4.24 z, August 2026, top decile. Window 2026-08-01 to 2027-02-01. Wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its record.
- **US dry-spell length** [N37]: -0.69 z, August 2026, the wetter side; two declared upstream paths land on price through it. Window 2026-08-31 to 2026-11-30. Wrong if it returns to the middle of its record.

Weighed and left: the stocks-to-use ratio [N11] and harvested area [N94] are both past declared lines, but their next print on 2026-10-09 restates a period already reported -- standing context inside a three-month horizon, not a watch item.
